title: Kobalos_Malware_Investigation_4b1
description: Investigate the Kobalos malware infection on the target network, identify malicious activity, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the Kobalos malware, a sophisticated Linux backdoor. Your task is to investigate the infection, identify the malicious activity, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and any connected hosts.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and any connected hosts.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: Investigate the `target` host and identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system.
levels.solution: Check the list of active services and look for any that seem unusual or unauthorized. Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` or `ps aux` to enumerate running services.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of active services and look for any that seem unusual or unauthorized.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` or `ps aux` to enumerate running services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service identified in the previous task is automatically started after reboot.
levels.solution: Examine systemd services and timers to find any that might be related to the suspicious service. Use commands like `systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled` or `ls /etc/systemd/system` to identify persistence mechanisms.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine systemd services and timers to find any that might be related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled` or `ls /etc/systemd/system` to identify persistence mechanisms.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Determine which network port is used for the suspicious communication between the `target` host and the `c2-server`.
levels.solution: Check the network connections and listen ports to find any unusual or unauthorized communication. Use commands like `ss -tulnp` or `netstat -tulnp` to identify suspicious ports.
